lenses.definition: Ukraine has sovereignty over all its internationally recognized territory; annexation has no legal recognition.

rules.support: Explicitly recognizes Ukrainian sovereignty over its internationally recognized territory/borders, or rejects legal annexation with a clearly specified territorial scope that actually answers the fixed proposition. Generic sovereignty or integrity language alone is insufficient.
rules.oppose: Explicitly recognizes legal Russian annexation or denies Ukrainian legal sovereignty over the territory named in the proposition. Reporting de facto control or a temporary ceasefire line alone is insufficient.
rules.no_stance: Generic invocations of sovereignty, territorial integrity or the UN Charter without resolving the relevant Ukrainian legal territory; peace talks; another country; partial territorial claims that do not settle the full target.
rules.mixed: Endorses and rejects the same Ukrainian legal territorial proposition within an inseparable passage. Split distinct regions/claims first and record scope instead of hiding it in one label.
rules.unresolved: Unclear whether territory refers to internationally recognized Ukrainian borders or a different line; unclear legal recognition versus temporary practical control.
examples: We recognize Ukraine’s sovereignty within its internationally recognized borders.
We recognize the annexed Ukrainian territories as legally part of Russia.
We accept and reject the very same annexation; this contradictory paragraph needs splitting.
Those borders should be respected. (Context does not identify which borders.)
rules.notes: Crimea/referendum material requires exact legal and territorial interpretation. Do not invent an all-territory stance from vague independence language. Qualified or region-specific claims should be preserved for scoped review, not generalized.

lenses.definition: Russian forces should withdraw from all internationally recognized Ukrainian territory.

rules.support: Calls for Russian forces to leave all internationally recognized Ukrainian territory; interpret explicit universal withdrawal in its supplied Ukrainian context.
rules.oppose: Explicitly endorses continued Russian military control/presence on that territory. A mere statement that forces are present is descriptive, not an endorsement.
rules.no_stance: Ceasefire, diplomacy, freezing fighting, NATO troop movements, withdrawal from another country, or reporting military activity without a withdrawal position.
rules.mixed: Inseparable endorsement and rejection of withdrawal under the same defined conditions; split different territories, actors and time windows first.
rules.unresolved: Unclear whose forces, which territory, whether removal is a demand or hypothetical, or whether a partial withdrawal satisfies the full target.
examples: Russian forces must withdraw from all internationally recognized Ukrainian territory.
Russian forces should permanently retain military control there. (There explicitly means Ukrainian territory.)
Both sides should hold peace talks.
Under identical conditions we demand full withdrawal and insist the occupation continue.
They should leave that area. (Forces and area are unidentified.)
rules.notes: A call to return to pre-February-2022 lines may leave Crimea unresolved. Do not silently equate it with withdrawal from all internationally recognized territory.

lenses.definition: Supports external military assistance to Ukraine, with type, recipient and conditions preserved.

rules.support: Explicitly endorses or supplies external military equipment, weapons, training or defined military support to Ukraine, retaining type, recipient and conditions. The specified assistance, not the country’s alliance, is the target.
rules.oppose: Explicitly opposes the defined external military assistance to Ukraine; refusal to provide it oneself need not oppose others providing it.
rules.no_stance: Humanitarian/economic aid alone; NATO deterrence deployments outside Ukraine; Ukraine’s abstract self-defence right without a commitment to military assistance; military activity concerning another country.
rules.mixed: Inseparable support and opposition to the same aid definition. Support for defensive arms but opposition to direct combat deployment should normally be split and qualified, not merged into a midpoint.
rules.unresolved: Assistance type, recipient, external supplier, modality or conditions are too unclear to decide whether the defined military policy is endorsed.
examples: We support supplying defensive weapons to Ukraine. (Record defensive-weapons scope.)
No state should supply weapons or military training to Ukraine.
We will provide food and medical relief to Ukraine.
We both support and oppose the same weapons transfer under the same conditions.
We will provide the necessary assistance. (Type not specified.)
rules.notes: Rejecting US combat deployment is not opposition to weapons aid. Do not generalize support for one bounded aid type to every possible weapon or intervention; preserve a narrower target rather than invent a blanket position.

lenses.definition: Supports specified restrictive measures against Russia because of its actions in Ukraine.

rules.support: Explicitly supports adopting or maintaining specified restrictive measures against Russia because of its actions in Ukraine. Preserve the measure, target, conditions and temporal state.
rules.oppose: Explicitly opposes adopting/maintaining those Russia-related measures or calls for their removal. Distinguish objections to one measure from all sanctions.
rules.no_stance: Sanctions on Cuba, Zimbabwe, terrorists or another target; descriptions of prices or humanitarian costs alone; a reporter asking about sanctions without an endorsed answer.
rules.mixed: Inseparable support and opposition to the same Russia/Ukraine-linked measure. Normally split different measures, exemptions, adoption and conditional removal.
rules.unresolved: The sanctioned target, Ukraine linkage, measure, stance or conditions are not identifiable from passage and context.
examples: We will maintain these restrictions on Russian banks in response to the invasion.
The invasion-related restrictions on Russian banks must be lifted now.
The embargo on Cuba should end.
We endorse and reject the same banking restriction without a coherent distinction.
These measures should stop. (Neither target nor measures is clear.)
rules.notes: An energy-payment exemption does not negate all sanctions. A threat to impose measures conditional on a future act must retain its condition; do not code it as enacted sanctions.

lenses.definition: Attributes responsibility for the February 2022 full-scale invasion to the Russian state.

rules.support: Explicitly attributes the February 2022 full-scale invasion to the Russian state, its government, military or leadership; identifying Russia as initiating the attack can establish attribution without the word responsibility.
rules.oppose: Explicitly rejects Russian-state responsibility for that invasion. A claim about shared background causes alone does not entail this rejection.
rules.no_stance: Generic conflict language, economic consequences, calls for peace, personal responsibility in another context, or an unendorsed account of another speaker’s claim.
rules.mixed: Inseparable assertion and rejection of Russian responsibility for the same invasion. Criticism of NATO alongside recognition that Russia initiated the invasion need not be mixed.
rules.unresolved: Unclear referent of attack/aggression, date, actor, quoted speaker, irony or whether the assertion concerns 2014 rather than the 2022 full-scale invasion.
examples: Russia initiated the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.
The Russian state bears no responsibility for that invasion.
The conflict has increased food prices.
Russia initiated this invasion and did not initiate it; both assertions remain unresolved in the passage.
They started it. (Neither actor nor event is identifiable.)
rules.notes: Not applicable before 24 February 2022. Rejecting a quoted Kremlin justification can reverse the apparent meaning of a quotation; read the surrounding context and request an expanded span when necessary.
